F01.author: model-n-claude
F01.confidence: medium — the arithmetic is exactly log.c's TranCommitted/EarlierPassno. It needs one log write to stay outstanding for a full lap: 4 pages in the model, at least 13 pages in a real log (elbl_MinLogSize with 8K blocks).
F01.defence: The model has the activeLogBlock-based commit test, which is the source's defence against out-of-order completion. Without it (D_ALB=FALSE, `mut_noalb`) a forced commit returns before its page lands even in the honest environment. With it in place, the page-offset wrap defeats it.
F01.effect: A transaction whose commit was acknowledged by a forced commit (fsync path) is rolled back by recovery (silent): breaks G7 and G23 (also G29). The same test gates buffer.c Write's log force (G5), but no WAL break was found within the bounds checked (see REPORT.md).
F01.heading: F3
F01.label: model-n-claude#3
F01.mechanism: TranCommitted and BufCommitted compare a position against (EarlierPassno(activeLogBlock), activeLogBlock), where activeLogBlock is the oldest page still in transit. When that page has the same index as currentLogBlock, EarlierPassno returns the current pass, so the stalled page looks a lap newer and every record behind it, including pages still in transit, counts as committed. elbl_ForceTran then returns without waiting, so elbt_TranForce(waitOK=1) returns for a transaction whose END page is not on disk. A crash loses that page, and recovery undoes the transaction.
F01.violated: The log device left one log-page write (page 0) outstanding while it completed enough later log writes for currentLogBlock to wrap round to the same page index, a full lap of the log.

F02.author: model-c-grok
F02.confidence: high — the trace ends recovered b1=2, oracle b1=1, cksum bad, version unknown, and the honest replay of the real log keeps 1.
F02.defence: The checksum routine is the defence, and it is enabled in this run. The unknown-version branch makes the check succeed and print that the checksum is being ignored. Removing the checksum defence also accepts the torn body (traces/C021-nodefence.txt). A known bad checksum is pulled back; this cell is the fail-open version.
F02.effect: Recovery finishes and writes a metadata value the disk did not commit. Users see block b1 as 2 rather than the committed 1. Breaks G54 and G1.
F02.heading: F4
F02.label: model-c-grok#4
F02.mechanism: The committed log records b1 changing from 0 to 1, and the home block is already 1. The page recovery reads has a bad checksum, an unknown checksum version, and a body that records the new value 2 together with an end record. ValidLogPageChecksum forces success on UNKNOWN_CKSUM_TYPE (recover.c:2577). The torn page is parsed instead of pulling the head back to the good prefix. Redo installs 2.

F03.author: model-n-claude
F03.confidence: medium — each step follows a source line (log.c elbl_InitLog, recover.c SafeDumpLog/MarkCommitted, tran.c elbt_GlobalTranId), but it needs out-of-order completion among the first pages after a mount, then a second crash before those pages are overwritten.
F03.defence: The model has the pass-number fence between log incarnations (IncPassno at open, +2 after recovery), the in-transit io_window check and the per-page pass check. The fence fails because two incarnations get the same pass when no recovery ran between them. The io_window check, which would catch the missing page 0, never runs because the log looks clean. Removing the fence (D_INC=FALSE) lets stale pages join a log with no environment deviation at all (`mut_noinc` fails). Removing D_IOW, D_PASS or D_BUMP leaves this run unchanged (`f1_noIOW`, `f1_noPASS`, `f1_noBUMP` fail the same way).
F03.effect: Recovery reports success but metadata now holds an update of a transaction that never ended (silent): breaks G3 and G8 (also G1, G2). The same mechanism can instead make recovery abort with RCVR_ASSERT on records left UNDEF (G55/G58; `model/results/v3/f1_fail.out`).
F03.heading: F1
F03.label: model-n-claude#1
F03.mechanism: Page 0 still holds the restart record, so elbl_InitLog (elbr_GetCleanLogInfo) treats the log as clean, skips recovery, and reopens it with passno = IncPassno(restart pass), the same pass the crashed incarnation used, so the stale page 1 cannot be told apart from the new incarnation's pages. After a second crash SafeDumpLog's binary search takes the stale page as head, its io_window and pass-number checks pass because page 0 now holds a new page with the same pass, and the stale records join the active log. MarkCommitted matches records by tran id alone and tran ids restart at 0xfffffff6 on every boot, so the stale END of boot-1 tran 1 marks boot-2 tran 1's uncommitted update REDO.
F03.violated: The log device completed a later write of a freshly opened log (page 1) before its first write (page 0, which overwrites the restart block), and the machine crashed in between; log.c ForceMap explicitly allows this ("We don't assume in-order writes").

F04.author: model-c-grok
F04.confidence: high — the trace ends recovered b1=0 and oracle b1=1 after the kill replaces the log, and the honest run keeps t1's redo.
F04.defence: elbb_Kill returns BUF_CANTDELETE only when metadataOK is false and the buffer is logged and dirty (buffer.c:1395). That boolean is the defence. It does not look at whether the freeing transaction's end record is durable. block_alloc.c:450 passes metadataOK true. The defence-removed run breaks the same way (traces/C024-nodefence.txt) because the true flag never consulted the commit record.
F04.effect: A committed metadata update is gone after the crash, while the uncommitted follower is undone. A later free can look committed in memory and then abort, resurrecting or dropping the block the committed transaction described. Breaks G7, G21, and G22.
F04.heading: F2
F04.label: model-c-grok#2
F04.mechanism: Transaction t1 commits an update of b1 from 0 to 1. The home block is still 0 because the dirty buffer is holding the redo in the active log. Transaction t2 then logs an update and does not commit. elbb_Kill with metadataOK true drops t1's buffer, and the active log that recovery sees no longer contains t1's redo (the model replaces that log with t2's record, which is the checkpoint moving past a buffer that left the age queue). Crash undoes t2 and has nothing to redo for t1, so b1 stays 0.

F05.author: model-c-claude
F05.confidence: medium — mechanism follows the source line by line; the overwrite must hit the newest pages before the crash.
F05.defence: checksums (ValidLogPageChecksum) and pass numbers detect the damage, but the head-window rule converts detected damage into "not yet written" instead of failing; only damage outside the window raises RCVR_IOERR.
F05.effect: a transaction fsync/LogForce reported as committed is silently lost after recovery; G7, G23 (Inv_Durable).
F05.heading: F-draft-1 (D24)
F05.label: model-c-claude#1
F05.mechanism: A completed, acknowledged log page at the head of the active log is overwritten (no magic, bad checksum). Recovery's binary search does not check magic on the endpoints, finds that page as head, and the in-transit window scan (recover.c:940-975) treats the checksum failure as an incomplete write, moving the head to the previous page. The committed transaction's END is discarded and its records are undone (or simply not redone), with no error.

F06.author: model-c-grok
F06.confidence: high — the trace ends recovered b1=0 and oracle b1=1, with the seen log containing only the update, and the honest run replays the end record and keeps 1.
F06.defence: SafeDumpLog checks the checksum and the pass number of the page it read (recover.c:933 and the active-page pass check). Both succeed for an older well-formed page. They do not detect that the end record was on the page the device should have returned. The defence-removed run undoes the same committed value (traces/C018-nodefence.txt).
F06.effect: A committed metadata update is undone after a stale read of the log head. Users see the pre-transaction value of b1. Breaks G7.
F06.heading: F5
F06.label: model-c-grok#5
F06.mechanism: The committed log is an update of b1 from 0 to 1 plus an end record, and the home block is already 1. The read of the head returns the previous well-formed page, which contains the update and not the end. Pass number and checksum both accept that page. Recovery classifies the transaction as undo, because it sees no end, and writes the old value 0 back over the committed home block.

F07.author: model-n-claude
F07.confidence: medium — direct consequence of recover.c step 5 and SafeDumpLog; needs two independent events (a hole at the first crash, then an interruption inside recovery's two-write window).
F07.defence: The model has recover.c's checkpoint-before-restart block ("the checkpoint block itself becomes the entire active region of the log") plus the head search (binary search, io_window, pass checks). Removing the checkpoint write (D_CKPT=FALSE, `f2_noCKPT`) removes every violation at the same bounds, so the checkpoint write is what turns a tolerated hole into corruption. Removing D_IOW does not change this run (`f2_noIOW`), because at N=4 the binary search, not the io_window check, stops at the hole.
F07.effect: After a successful recovery a transaction is partly applied, and an abort decided by one recovery is undone by the next (silent): breaks G2 and G6/G8 (also G1).
F07.heading: F2
F07.label: model-n-claude#2
F07.mechanism: The first recovery's head search stops at the hole and correctly undoes the transaction. It then writes its checkpoint block at head+1, which is the hole, with the same pass number and a valid checksum. On the next recovery the binary search therefore reaches the stale page 2 as head, and its io_window check sees only the valid checkpoint page. The transaction whose END is on page 2 is marked REDO even though its middle record (on the lost page 1) is gone, so only part of it is redone, reversing the first recovery's decision.
F07.violated: The log device kept one write (page 1) outstanding while it completed a later one (page 2, holding a transaction's END), and the machine crashed. Then a second crash (or a failed restart write followed by a rerun of recovery) interrupted elbr_Recover after elbr_WriteCheckpointBlock and before elbr_WriteRestartBlock.

F08.author: model-c-grok
F08.confidence: high — the trace ends with an empty log, recovered b1=1, and oracle b1=0, and the honest force keeps the log record ahead of the home write.
F08.defence: The log's check of the I/O status is the defence. It never observes ESOFT, because the async layer cleared the error first. With that check removed the same home block is still published (traces/C041-nodefence.txt).
F08.effect: A metadata write that the file system treated as logged is on disk, and the log that should undo it is not. After the crash users see the uncommitted value. Breaks G5 and G29.
F08.heading: F3
F08.label: model-c-grok#3
F08.mechanism: The update of b1 is logged in memory and the log force is the next step. On AIX, asevent_Iodone clears ESOFT, b_resid, and B_ERROR before the log looks at the event (asevent.c:1070). The force is therefore reported successful while the log page was not stored. Write-ahead then allows the home write, so disk b1 becomes 1. No end record is durable, so the committed image is still the old value. Crash sees an empty log and leaves b1 at 1.

F09.author: model-c-grok
F09.confidence: high — the trace ends recovered b1=1, oracle b1=0, with fake restart set, and the honest run of the same uncommitted image undoes it.
F09.defence: The clean test is the defence, and a well-formed restart is what it accepts. elbr_InitLogPageHdr already puts the salvage magic on every page, and the restart page is deliberately not checksummed, so a restored or forged restart is indistinguishable from a finished recovery. Removing the magic check does not help: the clean path is taken because the image looks like a restart, which traces/C058-nodefence.txt also shows.
F09.effect: After the crash the aggregate mounts as a clean log. Users see metadata the transaction did not commit. Breaks G56, G58, G8, and G1.
F09.heading: F1
F09.label: model-c-grok#1
F09.mechanism: An uncommitted update of block b1 from 0 to 1 is logged and its home block is written. The environment then plants a restart image on the first log block. elbr_GetCleanLogInfo (recover.c:2813 and recover.c:2840) treats salvage magic plus a first record of type restart as a clean log, and it does not checksum that page (recover.c:2826 and recover.c:2737). Replay never runs. The home block stays 1.

F10.author: model-c-claude
F10.defence: checksums detect the decay, but within the io_window range a bad page is taken to be an in-flight write and silently truncated.
F10.effect: acknowledged commits silently disappear; G7, G23.
F10.heading: F-draft-2 (D4)
F10.label: model-c-claude#2
F10.mechanism: Bits of a completed head log page decay (checksum fails, header intact). Recovery finds it as head by pass number; the in-transit scan (index 0 is the head itself) sees the bad checksum and pulls the head back one page, so the END of an acknowledged transaction is dropped and its updates are undone or not redone.

R28.label: codex-2/Limits and undecided points/13
R28.text: Performance claims G9–G11 are qualified by active log size, transaction duration, checkpointing, storage speed and available recovery memory; the paper's benchmark hardware is evidence for measured results, not a universal required device model. User-data atomicity is expressly excluded. Checksums are finite and may be disabled by the chosen supported format, so detection claims never imply arbitrary-corruption protection. No requirement of whole-page atomicity or in-order completion was inferred: the code explicitly tolerates out-of-order writes and partial pages in the in-transit window.
